newsitem.title: INDIA: No shortage of outcomes to India crisis.
newsitem.headline: No shortage of outcomes to India crisis.

text.p: India faced political gridlock on Thursday with a dizzying array of possible outcomes as a 12-day crisis headed towards a parliamentary vote of confidence.
Talks between the ruling United Front and the Congress party ended in deadlock and both formations said they would not budge from their irreconcilable positions.
Failing a last-minute deal, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda would be hard-pressed to win the confidence vote set for Friday evening in the lower house of parliament.
His 15-party centre-left coalition lacks an absolute majority and without Congress's support could not withstand parliament's biggest party, the rightwing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The most straightforward outcome would have the prime minister go down to defeat, putting an end to his 10 months in power. But his defeat could lead to a myriad of other scenarios.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma could turn to the BJP, which held power for 12 days last May before failing to muster a majority. But the president could also tap a leader of another party.

Congress appeared to be banking on the possibility that the United Front would be prepared to negotiate a power-sharing deal without Deve Gowda but with either the United Front or Congress at the helm.
If no alliance proved capable of achieving a majority, the second elections in a year would become inevitable.
A senior United Front official said the coalition was prepared for polls in May or June under a caretaker government headed by Deve Gowda.

Some politicians suggested Congress and the United Front could reach an agreement before the parliamentary vote. Under one scenario, Deve Gowda would resign and the two formations then would ask the president to name their choice as the next leader.

Speculation on a possible compromise choice earlier this week centred on G.K. Moopanar, a former Congress member from the southern state of Tamil Nadu who broke away last year to form the Tamil Maanila Congress.
But Moopanar has appeared to show little interest in the prime minister's post.
The impetus for a tie-up between the United Front and Congress would be their common fear of general elections which opinion surveys show would bolster the BJP.
One scenario had the BJP handing victory to Deve Gowda by abstaining in the vote, in hopes that differences between the United Front and Congress would then fester -- to the Hindu party's advantage.
